title: Corporate Pricing — Product Group Override: multi-dot numeric input ('1.2.3') silently coerced to valid number ('1.23') with no validation error
requirementSource: NM-1463 (Corporate PG Pricing Override Management & Context Filtering) — standard input-validation expectation: a value that is not a valid decimal number must be rejected or flagged; silent coercion of malformed input to a plausible-looking number is a data-integrity defect.
stepsToReproduce: Open Corporate Pricing > Product Group Override for an office that has override data (e.g., cloudapps-e2e.encoreglobal.com/navigator/locations/1606/settings/corporate-pricing/pg-override).
In the 'Change Local Office' picker, search '1606', check the row, and click 'Select' to load the office's overrides.
In the override grid, click into an Override Price or Max Discount % cell to enter edit mode.
Clear the current value and type '1.2.3' (a string with two decimal points — an invalid numeric input).
Press Tab or click elsewhere to commit the value.
Observe what value is stored in the cell and whether any validation error or warning is shown.
expectedBehavior: Entering '1.2.3' is either rejected with a visible validation error (e.g. 'Must be a valid number') or the field reverts to its prior value. The malformed input must never be silently committed as a different, plausible-looking number.
actualBehavior: The value '1.2.3' is silently coerced to '1.23' — the second decimal point and trailing digit are stripped, producing a number that looks valid but differs from what the user typed. No validation error or warning is shown. The user cannot detect the silent change unless they notice the committed value has changed.

mcpEvidence.findings: Field inventory records: Override Price, Max Discount % — '1.2.3' typed → '1.23' committed — typo silently becomes a plausible number. Observed during systematic field census on the override screen.
